question: Yesterday, the WHO declared an international health emergency due to an increase in cases of Mpox (160 %) in a number of African countries. In the face of a new international health crisis, once again we are adopting a reactive approach and still do not have an agreement to fall back on during pandemics that would allow the transfer of technologies to lower income countries.
Yesterday, the Commission announced that 215 000 doses of the MVA-BN vaccine would be donated, which is a positive step, albeit a clearly insufficient one.

An effective strategy will require millions of doses of the vaccine to be made available, the reinforcement of EU-Africa coordination measures for prevention and epidemiological control, and capacity building in low-income countries, to ensure access to diagnosis, treatment and vaccines, as well as the distribution and implementation of the latter. In the light of the above: 1.
What urgent measures does the Commission intend to take to cooperate with the African authorities in monitoring the situation in the countries concerned?

With a view to improving the current situation and also preventing future health crises, how will the Commission help to ensure the transfer of technologies, the development of local production and the strengthening of health and epidemiological systems in lowincome countries?
What steps have been taken by HERA and the ECDC with regard to the monitoring of Mpox in Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.11.2024) 1. Following the donation to Africa Centres for Disease Control (AfCDC) of 215 420 vaccine doses, the Commission is preparing a EUR 9.4 million action with the AfCDC to strengthen diagnostic/sequencing capacities against mpox.

It has mobilised EUR 1 million to support the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) from the Epidemics tool and EUR 200 000 from humanitarian assistance to Burundi. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) has deployed staff to the DRC to support surveillance through the AfCDC-ECDC Partnership. 2.

The Commission is contributing EUR 462 million to the Pandemic Fund, to support surveillance and early warning projects in ten countries impacted by mpox. The Commission is also supporting the African Vaccine Manufacturing Accelerator launched by the Vaccine Alliance ‘GAVI’1 in June 2024, and the Team Europe Initiative on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies in Africa.

The latter aims to increase vaccine manufacturing in Africa and has mobilised EUR 1.3 billion for that purpose. 3. The Commission and the Member States coordinate the response to mpox through the Health Security Committee. The ECDC monitors the epidemiological situation through its global epidemic intelligence activities and published a Rapid Risk Assessment on 16 August 20242.

The ‘Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Authority’ (HERA) is funding DURABLE3, which has contributed to the biological characterisation of clade Ib4 and developed a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay able to detect this clade. HERA and ECDC performed a joint survey to ensure that the EU has the diagnostic capacities to detect the potential introduction of clade Ib in the EU.
